item.title: The copper peptide trend has gone from creams to injections — ahead of the science
item.description: Copper peptides are among the biggest viral trends on social media. Does evidence support smearing on the electric blue tincture for firmer skin, wound healing and other anti-aging effects?

item.title: Pig kidneys keep patients alive long enough to get human kidneys for the first time
item.description: For the first time, genetically modified pig kidneys keep two kidney failure patients alive long enough to get human kidneys.

item.title: Rewriting the narrative: One man's journey through the new era of lung cancer care
item.description: Lung cancer is still the top cancer killer. But new developments are shifting what the future might hold for patients, as one man's cancer journey shows.

item.title: Whatever happened to the floating schools of Bangladesh?
item.description: It was a light bulb moment: If monsoon rains keep kids from safely getting to school, let's create a floating school to pick them up! Bangladesh pioneered the idea. How's it doing?

item.title: Whatever happened to the U.S. campaign to ban child marriage?
item.description: The global effort to end child marriage is in the news. In the U.S., there's a new bill before Congress (but it's controversial). And the U.N. is designating a day dedicated to ending the practice.
